claims.claim: PyTorch 2.15: scaled_dot_product_attention with a boolean lower-triangle attn_mask equals is_causal=True; True means take part; editing the last position leaves earlier causal outputs unchanged; nn.MultiheadAttention gives padded keys weight 0.0 when key_padding_mask is True there; a fully masked row returned zeros from scaled_dot_product_attention on CPU, and nan in a NumPy softmax.
claims.source: Run on PyTorch 2.15.0 (PyPI wheel, CPU) and NumPy, November 2026.

concept_html:
Two kinds of position must stay out of attention.

Padding. Padded positions (lesson B25-L1) carry no text. Set their scores to minus infinity before softmax, so their weights become exactly 0 and every query ignores them.

The future. A model that predicts the next token must not read it. A causal mask lets position i attend to positions 0 to i only: keep the lower triangle, np.tril(np.ones((L, L), dtype=bool)). Row 0 then puts all its weight on itself.

scores = np.where(allowed, scores, -np.inf)    # allowed: True where attention may look

Two opposite conventions in PyTorch 2.15:

  • F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=allowed) takes a boolean mask where True means take part. is_causal=True builds the causal mask for you, and gave the same outputs as the lower-triangle mask.
  • nn.MultiheadAttention(...)(q, k, v, key_padding_mask=is_pad) takes a mask where True means ignore this key. In a check, padded keys received weight 0.0.

Passing one function's mask to the other inverts it, with no error. Name each mask by its meaning, allowed or is_pad, and flip it with ~ where needed.

Test it. A causal model's output at position t must not change when a later token changes. In a check, editing the last position's value left every earlier output unchanged. Padding passes the same test: adding pads must not change the outputs at real positions.

Every query needs an allowed key. In NumPy, a row with every key masked gives nan. scaled_dot_product_attention on a CPU returned zeros for such rows, a quieter failure. Pad on the right and keep each position allowed to see itself.

lines: import numpy as np
def causal_padding_mask(ids: np.ndarray, pad_id: int = 0) -> np.ndarray:
"""Allowed attention for one right-padded sequence: past or present, never padding.
Args:
ids: Token IDs, shape (length,), padding only at the end.
pad_id: The padding ID.
Returns:
Boolean (length, length): True where query i may attend to key j.
Raises:
ValueError: If ids is not 1-D or starts with padding.
"""
if ids.ndim != 1 or len(ids) == 0 or ids[0] == pad_id:
raise ValueError("need a non-empty 1-D sequence that starts with a real token")
causal = np.tril(np.ones((len(ids), len(ids)), dtype=bool))
return causal & (ids != pad_id)[None, :]
def masked_attention(Q: np.ndarray, K: np.ndarray, V: np.ndarray, allowed: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
"""Attention where allowed is False gets zero weight."""
scores = np.where(allowed, Q @ K.T / np.sqrt(Q.shape[-1]), -np.inf)
scores = scores - scores.max(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
weights = np.exp(scores)
return (weights / weights.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)) @ V

exercises.solution:
import numpy as np


def masked_attention(Q: np.ndarray, K: np.ndarray, V: np.ndarray, allowed: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Scaled dot-product attention where allowed is False gets zero weight.

    Args:
        Q: Queries, shape (n_queries, d).
        K: Keys, shape (n_keys, d).
        V: Values, shape (n_keys, d_v).
        allowed: Boolean, shape (n_queries, n_keys). True where attention may look.

    Returns:
        Outputs, shape (n_queries, d_v).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the mask has the wrong shape or a row allows no key.
    """
    if allowed.shape != (len(Q), len(K)):
        raise ValueError(f"mask {allowed.shape} does not match ({len(Q)}, {len(K)})")
    if not allowed.any(axis=1).all():
        raise ValueError("every query needs at least one allowed key")
    scores = np.where(allowed, Q @ K.T / np.sqrt(Q.shape[-1]), -np.inf)
    scores = scores - scores.max(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    weights = np.exp(scores)
    return (weights / weights.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)) @ V

title: Masks for padding and for the future
why_html: A model that drafted the next word of a survey answer reached a near-perfect validation loss within an hour, then produced nonsense when used. Its attention had no causal mask, so during training every position could read the word it was asked to predict. The test "change a later token, check earlier outputs stay the same" would have failed on the first run.
